memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"The LORD said to Moses and Aaron in Egypt, 'This month is to be for you the
first month, the first month of your year.'" - Ex 12:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Before God delivers His people, He resets their calendar. That is a striking
place to start. You would expect instructions about packing, or routes, or
weapons. Instead God says: from now on, count your years from here.

Israel had a calendar already. Egypt had one too, tied to the Nile and the
harvest. But God says the year now begins with redemption. Everything before
this is the old reckoning. Everything after is measured from the night He set
them free.

Notice also where this is spoken: "in Egypt." They are still slaves. Nothing has
visibly changed. Yet God speaks to them as a people with their own calendar,
their own future, their own national life. He names what will be before it is.

This is how God works with us as well. When a person comes to Christ, there is a
line drawn. Paul writes, "If anyone is in Christ, the new creation has come: The
old has gone, the new is here!" (2 Cor 5:17). That is not merely poetic. It is a
real reordering of how our life is counted.

You may still be surrounded by the old circumstances. But if you belong to
Christ, God has already started your calendar over.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. From what point do you measure your life?
2. Is there an "old reckoning" you are still living by?
3. How would today look if you truly believed the new has come?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, thank You that in Christ You have given me a new beginning. Help me to
live today from that new starting point rather than from my old life. Amen.
